question_text: A design company needs shared storage with unpredictable demand. Option P is cloud storage dedicated to the company, managed by its own team. Option Q is a provider-managed cloud service sharing infrastructure among customers with logical separation. Evaluate the options in terms of control, cost, scalability and suitability.
adaptation_rationale: Define the two deployments in the prompt and assess cloud infrastructure trade-offs, not unsupported model-taxonomy recall. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: P gives more direct configuration/control but needs the company to fund/manage capacity and expertise. Q can provide elastic capacity and avoid much local administration, but ongoing fees, provider dependence and data-location/access controls need review. For fluctuating demand with a small support team, Q may be suitable if its contractual/security controls meet requirements; unusually strict control needs could justify P.

marking_points.criterion: Explains dedicated option’s greater direct control/customization.
Discusses provider fee, dependence or data-control limitation.
Makes a justified scenario-based choice balancing the options.
